title: Keep TypeScript function nesting depth at or below 4

facts.note: Applies to every TypeScript/TSX function in scanned source, regardless of change status or phase.
TS/TSX source files; the source's categorical exclusions are test files and vendored/build directories (exact classification is the detector's).

fires: Any scanned non-test .ts/.tsx function of 3+ code lines reaches control-flow nesting depth 5 (e.g. an if inside a for inside a try inside a switch inside an if), whether newly written, edited, or pre-existing.
An edit adds a nested conditional to a function already at depth 4.
Illustrative: the Bun metrics detector reports COMPLEXITY-NESTING-TS-001 for a function (a finding is evidence of violation, not a prerequisite for the obligation).
doesNotFire: A function with fewer than 3 code lines.
Code in test files or in vendored/build directories.
Brace depth that occurs only on lines without a control keyword (e.g. nested object literals) or only in comments.

given: Any TypeScript/TSX function of 3+ code lines outside test files and vendored/build directories
when: it is present in scanned source
then: Keep its maximum control-flow nesting depth (control_depth) at or below 4.
prefer: Invert conditions into early-return guard clauses when that preserves cleanup, error, and ordering semantics.
Extract a cohesive inner operation into a named function with a small, meaningful input.
Prepare or filter a collection before iterating when that makes the algorithm clearer.
Flatten control flow by removing unnecessary conditional context: first find early-reject conditions (guards), a cohesive inner block, nested iteration expressible as preparation plus one clear pass.
avoid: Clever boolean/ternary rewrites, brace removal, or re-encoding the same nesting solely to evade the depth count.
Extracting a block that needs a long parameter list or still depends on the caller's hidden conditional context.
Duplicating cleanup, logging, or error handling across new guard clauses.
Changing evaluation order or exception behavior while flattening.
why: At depth five a reader must hold five simultaneous conditions to know whether a line runs, beyond reliable working memory; depth is a sensor for too much conditional context. A guard or extracted helper usually removes a level without changing behaviour, so the threshold is enforced, not advised.
evidence: Existing behavior and tests remain green, including error and boundary paths.
The triggering nesting violation (COMPLEXITY-NESTING-TS-001) is gone in a bun_ts_metrics_detector run.
The flattened flow reads with fewer simultaneous preconditions (reviewer judgement).
Extracted functions satisfy the applicable length and complexity conventions.
The refactor introduces no new ATDD Bun violations.
verifier_detail: Threshold: violation when a function's control_depth > 4 (allowed max 4).
control_depth = maximum brace depth reached on lines carrying a control keyword (if / else / for / while / do / switch / try / catch / finally), measured relative to the function's own base depth.
Functions with fewer than 3 code lines are not scored.
Comment lines are ignored when measuring brace balance.
Test files and vendored/build directories are outside the scan.
Detector: bun_ts_metrics_detector (validator); finding alias COMPLEXITY-NESTING-TS-001; severity 3.
The goal is easier-to-understand execution conditions; a fix that only removes braces or encodes the same nesting in expressions the metric counts differently is metric gaming, not compliance.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Stack-neutral obligation; NATIVE BUN detector transcribed from the python-pytest sibling coder.refactor.complexity-nesting-typescript and verified numerically identical.
Alias COMPLEXITY-NESTING-TS-001 is the shared core alias (metadata.aliases).
Term guard_clause: an inverted condition returning early; the usual way to remove a level without changing behaviour.

sharedNodes.text: Strict disposition: atdd-bun fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.justification: Required by the output shape; derived directly from the source's depth definition and exceptions. No operation/phase gates are added; the obligation is universal over scored functions.
Marks that this verify item is not mechanically checkable.

trace.note: Corrective instruction: flatten by removing unnecessary conditional context
